$comment: Cross-language conformance fixture for the Content-Type a body mode implies when the request declares none (issue #2464). Read by the engine gtest suite (engine/tests/implied_content_type_test.cpp, via VAYU_ENGINE_SOURCE_DIR), which checks `vayu::http::implied_content_type` on the request each row describes; the app reads the same rows to pin its own copies of the table (the Body panel's mode list, the header row the panel writes, the code generators). `modes` holds exactly one row per body mode, with a body that has something to send: `expected` is the engine's implied type, "" when it implies none (`none` sends no body; `form-data` is libcurl's to write, `multipart/form-data` with the boundary it generates). `panelWritesRow` says whether the Body panel writes that type as a header row (true) or the engine derives it at send time with no row (false); it is the app's half and the engine does not read it. `cases` are the edge rows the engine answers differently from its mode row: an empty body, the GraphQL GET transport (the document travels in the URL, so there is no body to describe), and the binary tiers (declared type, then extension, then `application/octet-stream`). Row shape: `name`, `mode` (the payload spelling), `method` (default POST), and the body members a payload carries (`content`, `fields`, `file`). A typed Content-Type row still wins over every answer here, and `disabledSystemHeaders` removes it; neither is this table's question.

modes.name: binary with no declared type or known extension

cases.name: an empty text body has nothing to describe
an empty json body has nothing to describe
a form with no enabled field has nothing to describe
a text body on a GET is still text/plain
a text body on a PUT is still text/plain
graphql on a GET travels in the URL
binary names its declared type first
binary falls back to what its extension names
